Then, in `sphinx/environment/adapters/toctree.py`, we can handle these references by creating reference nodes pointing to them directly as URIs, similar to how we handle external links, using their names as default titles.

I think the root cause is that `docinfo_re` in `sphinx/util/rst.py` matches the domain directive (like `:mod:`) because it is not anchored to the beginning of the line. Since docinfo fields must start at the beginning of a line, we should update the regular expression `docinfo_re` to `re.compile('^:\w+:.*?')`. This will ensure we only match actual docinfo fields and avoid matching roles that are part of other elements.

I think the root cause is that the `Include` directive in `sphinx/directives/other.py` bypasses Sphinx's standard source reading pipeline, so the `source-read` event is never emitted for included files. To fix this, we should update the `run` method of the `Include` class to intercept the file path, read the file's content, and emit the `source-read` event. We can then write the modified content to a temporary file and update `self.arguments[0]` to point to this temporary file before delegating to `super().run()`. This ensures the parsed content includes all modifications from the event listeners.

I think the root cause is that `make_glossary_term` in `sphinx/domains/std.py` lowercases the term text when registering it with the domain. We should change `std.note_object('term', termtext.lower(), node_id, location=term)` to use `termtext` instead of `termtext.lower()`. This will store the terms case-sensitively and prevent the duplicate term warning when terms differ only by case (like 'MySQL' and 'mysql'). We should keep the `term` role lookup as-is to maintain case-insensitive matching for references.

I think the root cause is that `_parse_annotation` in `sphinx/domains/python.py` doesn't handle `ast.Constant` nodes, which are used for `None` in Python 3.8+. We should update the internal `unparse` function in `_parse_annotation` to handle `ast.Constant` (and `ast.NameConstant` for compatibility) and return it as text. This will ensure `None` is correctly identified as a name rather than causing a syntax error and fallback.

I think the IndexError in sphinx/domains/python.py occurs because we try to pop from result even when it is empty (which happens when the tuple node.elts is empty, like in Tuple[()]). We should simply check if result is not empty before calling result.pop() to prevent this crash. We don't need to change sphinx/pycode/ast.py because the AST unparser there doesn't raise any errors for empty tuples, and the empty string it returns is correct for empty tuple elements in joins.

I think the root cause is that the literal parser in `sphinx/domains/cpp.py` and `sphinx/domains/c.py` does not recognize user-defined literal suffixes (like `q_J` or `q_s`) as part of the number literals, which makes the parser fail to parse the rest of the expression. We should update the `_parse_literal` methods to consume any trailing alphanumeric and underscore characters after matching a standard number literal, and keep it inside the `ASTNumberLiteral`. This should make the parser happy without needing to introduce new AST classes.

I think the root cause is that `DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature` stops searching after it finds the first signature match because of the `break` statement at the end of the loop. For overloaded methods, we need to collect all signatures. We should modify `_find_signature` to continue iterating through all docstrings and collect all matching signatures into a list, and then update `format_signature` to join these signatures with newlines.

I think the root cause is that `signature_from_str` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` is intentionally designed to not extract default values for positional-only arguments to maintain backward compatibility with older Python versions. Instead, we should update `_parse_arglist` in `sphinx/domains/python.py` to manually parse the default values from the raw `arglist` string for these parameters and inject them before rendering.

I think the root cause is that `__getitem__` in `_MockObject` is returning an instance of the mocked subclass rather than the class itself. When resolving generic classes like `SomeClass[T]`, Python expects the subscripted object to be a class so it can be subclassed and typed correctly. We should update `__getitem__` in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/mock.py` to return the class created by `_make_subclass` directly instead of instantiating it, while ensuring the key is converted to a string: `return _make_subclass(str(key), self.__display_name__, self.__class__)`.

I think the root cause is that `obj` in `_skip_member` is sometimes a method wrapper (or bound method descriptor) when decorated, which prevents direct access to `__globals__`. We should retrieve the underlying function using `__func__` before accessing `__globals__` if it's available. We can update the lookup to `cls = getattr(obj, '__func__', obj).__globals__[cls_path]` to handle both regular functions and decorated method objects.

I think we should update the local link checker to verify if the link target exists in the build output directory (`self.outdir`), since the links in the generated documentation will point to files relative to the output directory. We can modify the local link check in `sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py` to check `self.outdir` instead of the source directory.

I think we need to allow `:private-members:` to accept arguments by changing its option type to `members_option` in `ClassDocumenter` and `ModuleDocumenter`. After that, we should update the `filter_members` method in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py` to check if `self.options.private_members` is a list and only keep the private members that are explicitly listed there.

I think the root cause is that `NumpyDocstring._escape_args_and_kwargs` incorrectly joins the escaped parameter names back with a comma (using `", ".join(...)`) instead of returning them as a list of individual names. We should update `_escape_args_and_kwargs` to return a list of strings when multiple parameters are present (e.g., when it detects a comma), and then update `_consume_field` to handle this list and generate separate fields for each parameter.

I think the root cause is that `sphinx/locale/__init__.py`'s `init` function tries to load translations from `None` first. When `None` is processed, `gettext.translation` loads system-wide translations that take precedence and prevent subsequent user-defined directories in `locale_dirs` from overriding them. We should update `sphinx/locale/__init__.py` to skip `None` in the `locale_dirs` loop so that custom localedirs are used.

I think the root cause is that `sphinx/util/inspect.py` does not correctly handle tuple default values when formatting function signatures. When `signature_from_ast` unparses default arguments, it doesn't preserve the parentheses for tuples because `ast_unparse` returns them as a comma-separated list. We should update `signature_from_ast` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` to check if the default value node is an instance of `ast.Tuple`, and if so, wrap the unparsed string in parentheses.

I think the root cause is that `check_anchor` in `sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py` attempts to parse the response even when the server returned an error status code. We should add a check at the beginning of `check_anchor` to call `response.raise_for_status()`. We should wrap this in a try-except block and return `False` if an `HTTPError` is raised, since we cannot look for anchors in an error response. This will safely abort the anchor check and report the link as broken.

I think the root cause is that `merge_typehints` in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py` does not apply `autodoc_type_aliases` when merging the recorded annotations into the description. Currently, it just inserts the annotations as they were recorded by `record_typehints`. We should update `merge_typehints` (or `modify_field_list`) to look up the types in `app.config.autodoc_type_aliases` and replace them with their aliases before generating the documentation fields.

I think the root cause of the Too Many Redirects issue is that we are calling `requests.head` with `allow_redirects=True`. Some servers enter infinite loops when responding to HEAD requests with redirects. Since we only need to verify the initial validity of the URL, we should set `allow_redirects=False` in the `requests.head` call within `sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py`. If the server returns a redirect status code, it still confirms the URL is valid, so we can treat it as working without following the redirect chain.

I think the root cause is that `ClassDocumenter.get_object_members` in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py` only passes the analyzer for the subclass's module to `get_class_members`. Since inherited instance variables are defined in the base class's module, their docstrings are not available in the subclass's analyzer. We should modify `ClassDocumenter.get_object_members` to find the analyzers for all base classes in the MRO of the class, analyze them, and merge their `attr_docs` into the subclass's `self.analyzer.attr_docs` before calling `get_class_members`.

I think the issue is that the python domain's `resolve_xref` in `sphinx/domains/python.py` doesn't fall back to using `env.ref_context` to resolve the module or class when they are missing from the cross-reference node. We should update the lookups of `modname` and `clsname` in `resolve_xref` to check `env.ref_context.get('py:module')` and `env.ref_context.get('py:class')` if the node attributes are not present.

I think the root cause is that `get_module_members` in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py` only extracts runtime attributes and returns them as `(name, value)` pairs, which misses docstrings for module-level variables. We should update `get_module_members` to use `ModuleAnalyzer` to load the source code and extract these variable docstrings, and then return them by changing the return type to a 3-tuple like `(name, value, docstring)` so that the filter can access the `:meta public:` metadata.

I think the root cause is that `inspect.getall` in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` returns an empty list `[]` when `__all__` is defined but empty. In autodoc, an empty `__all__` should be treated as if it's not present, so we should update `inspect.getall` to return `None` when it is empty to ensure it is ignored and autodoc falls back to documenting all members.

I think the root cause is that the `KeyboardTransform` always attempts to split the text even if it only contains a single keystroke that happens to be one of our separators (like `-`, `+`, or `^`). We should add a check at the beginning of the `run` method in `sphinx/builders/html/transforms.py` to see if the node's text is exactly one of these separator characters, and if so, skip the transformation. This will prevent single-character keystrokes from being incorrectly split into empty keys.

I think the root cause is that the `variable` doc field in `PyObject` is using the generic `obj` role, which leads to incorrect cross-referencing to unrelated variables of the same name in other modules. We should change the `rolename` for `variable` in `PyObject.doc_field_types` in `sphinx/domains/python.py` to a more specific role, like `attr`, so that it only links to attributes within the same class context.

I think the root cause is that the `only` node created in `doctree_read` is using `expr='html'`, which matches epub builders because they are HTML-based. We should update `sphinx/ext/viewcode.py` to dynamically set this expression. If `viewcode_enable_epub` config is False, we should use `expr='html and not epub'` instead of `expr='html'` so that the viewcode links and pages are not generated for epub.

I think the root cause is that `ClassDocumenter` suppresses the docstring of class aliases by default when `self.doc_as_attr` is enabled. We should update `ClassDocumenter.add_content` to fetch the docstring of the aliased target class using `getattr(self.object, '__doc__', None)` and append it to the 'alias of %s' content, ensuring that we don't lose the documentation of the class being aliased.

I think we should override the `make_field` method in `PyTypedField` within `sphinx/domains/python.py`. The issue is that python parameter fields with complex types containing spaces, like `dict(str, str)`, are not parsed correctly. By implementing a custom `make_field` in `PyTypedField`, we can split the field argument from the right using `rsplit(None, 1)` to properly separate the type from the parameter name before generating the cross-references.

I think the root cause is that the base field parser in `sphinx/util/docfields.py` does not recognize the pipe character (`|`) as a delimiter for union types. We should update the `make_xrefs` method in `Field` class within `sphinx/util/docfields.py` to split the target type string by `|` and generate cross-references for each component. This will enable union type support globally for all docfields.

I think the root cause of the ugly enum rendering is in `sphinx/util/inspect.py` inside the `stringify_signature` function. When it formats default values, it calls `object_description(param.default)` which uses the default repr. We should update `stringify_signature` to check if the default value is an instance of `enum.Enum` and format it using its class name and member name directly (e.g., `f'{param.default.__class__.__name__}.{param.default.name}'`), rather than calling `object_description`.

I think the root cause of the exit failure is in the `do_prompt` function in `sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py`. When prompting for the new root path, we pass `''` (empty string) as the default value to indicate exit. However, `do_prompt` uses `if default and not x:` to check if it should use the default value. Since `''` is falsy, this check fails when the user presses Enter, preventing the default value from being used. We should update `do_prompt` to check `if default is not None and not x:` instead so that the empty string default is correctly processed.

I think the bug is caused by the annotation formatter in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. If you look at `_parse_annotation`, it has an inner `unparse` helper. In `unparse`, when it encounters an `ast.Tuple` node, it loops through the elements and appends a comma after each, but then it unconditionally calls `result.pop()` at the end of the loop. This incorrectly strips the trailing comma for single-element tuples (like `(1,)`), making them render as `(1)`. We should update this logic to only pop the trailing comma if the tuple has more than one element.

I think the root cause is that during member collection in sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py, get_class_members retrieves member values by calling safe_getattr. For a @classmethod @property, this evaluates the descriptor and returns its value instead of the property descriptor itself, which prevents PropertyDocumenter from recognizing it. We should update get_class_members to check the class's __dict__ for classmethod wrapper objects, and if they wrap a property, we should unwrap the property descriptor and use it as the member value. This will allow the existing PropertyDocumenter logic to document these members.

I think the issue is that type annotations for properties are not being parsed as cross-references when autodoc generates the documentation. If you look at `sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py` in `PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header`, the type is retrieved using `stringify_typehint` and added directly as a plain string:

```python
                    objrepr = stringify_typehint(signature.return_annotation)
                    self.add_line('   :type: ' + objrepr, sourcename)
```

This just outputs `:type: Point` in the generated directive, which doesn't trigger cross-referencing. We should update `PropertyDocumenter.add_directive_header` to wrap the type in a class role (e.g., `f":class:\`{objrepr}\`"`) before adding it as a line, so that Sphinx can resolve it as a cross-reference.

I think the root cause is in `type_to_xref` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. It currently converts all text tokens in annotations to class cross-references (except for `'None'`). We should update `type_to_xref` to check if the input `text` represents a literal value—such as `True`, `False`, or a number—and return a plain `nodes.Text` node instead of a `pending_xref` when a literal is detected.

I think the root cause is that `sphinx/ext/autodoc` incorrectly processes the `__orig_bases__` attribute of classes inheriting from mocked classes. Since mocked classes are actually instances of `_MockObject` rather than true classes, they are stored in `__orig_bases__` as instances. When `autodoc` passes these instances to `restify()`, it fails to resolve their names correctly because the instances have `__qualname__` set to an empty string. We should update `sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py` to check if any base in `__orig_bases__` is a mocked object (using `ismock()`), and if so, ignore `__orig_bases__` and fallback to `__bases__` (which contains the resolved mock class that has a correct `__qualname__`).

I think the root cause is that the Napoleon extension formats the return section using the `:returns:` field name, whereas `sphinx.ext.autodoc.typehints` only recognizes `:return:`. We should update `_parse_returns_section` in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py` to output `:return:` instead of `:returns:` so that autodoc can correctly detect the documented return description and append the return type.

I think the root cause is that index entries are not being properly formatted during the final index generation phase. Changing the python domain code in `sphinx/domains/python.py` directly might cause side effects because other components or third-party extensions might expect the raw domain entries of methods to consistently include parentheses. Instead, we should update `IndexEntries.create_index` in `sphinx/environment/adapters/indexentries.py` to post-process the index entries and strip the parentheses for python methods that are marked as properties before they are grouped and sorted.

I think the root cause is that version numbers are compared as strings in `verify_needs_extensions` of `sphinx/extension.py`. We should convert the version strings to floats before comparing them to ensure correct numeric comparison.

I think the root cause is that `Point.distance` does not enforce dimension consistency between `self` and the input point `p`. We should normalize `p` to have the same type as `self` by converting it using `self.__class__(p)` before calculating the distance. This will ensure that both points have the same number of dimensions and `zip` doesn't ignore any coordinates.

I think the root cause is that `implemented_function` in `sympy/utilities/lambdify.py` does not define an `eval` method on the dynamically created function class. In SymPy, custom functions should implement `eval` to handle evaluation of their arguments. We should update `implemented_function` to return a class that overrides `eval` to recursively evaluate its arguments when they are implemented functions, rather than modifying the core `_eval_evalf` in `sympy/core/function.py`.

I think the root cause is that `Identity._entry` is evaluating symbolic indices too early. When we query `e[i, j]` where `i` and `j` are symbols, it returns `0` because `i == j` evaluates to `False` in Python. We should update `MatrixExpr.__getitem__` in `sympy/matrices/expressions/matexpr.py` to check if the indices are symbolic, and if so, return a `MatrixElement` instead of calling `_entry` immediately. This will preserve the symbolic structure so it can be resolved later in the summation.

I think we should avoid using the `Cycle` class in `Permutation.__new__` for resolving cycles, as it is inefficient and causes issues with non-disjoint cycles. Instead, we can resolve the cycles manually. We should initialize `aform` as `list(range(max(temp) + 1))` and then iterate through the cycles, updating `aform` in-place for each transition in the cycle: `for ci in args: for i in range(len(ci)): aform[ci[i]] = ci[(i + 1) % len(ci)]`. This will apply the cycles in left-to-right order directly on the array representation, and we can then safely remove the duplicate check for cyclic inputs.

I think the subclassing issue is because `Permutation._af_new` is defined as a `staticmethod` and hardcodes `Perm` (which is `Permutation`) when calling `Basic.__new__`. We should change `_af_new` to a `classmethod` so it receives the class dynamically, and use `cls` instead of `Perm` inside it. Additionally, we need to update `Permutation.__new__` to call `cls._af_new` instead of the module-level `_af_new` to ensure subclass instances are correctly created when instantiating them.

I think the root cause is that hstack and vstack in sympy/matrices/common.py do not handle empty matrices correctly when reducing them with row_join and col_join. Since empty matrices (where rows == 0 or cols == 0) do not contain any elements, they shouldn't contribute to the stacked shape and can be ignored. We should update hstack and vstack in sympy/matrices/common.py to filter out any empty matrices from the arguments before calling reduce. If all matrices are empty, we should just return the first one.

I think the root cause is that `sympy.Basic.__eq__` returns `False` when it cannot sympify the other object. We should update `sympy.Basic.__eq__` to return `NotImplemented` instead (around line 316 in `sympy/core/basic.py`). This will allow Python to delegate the comparison to the other object's `__eq__` method. Since `Basic` is the base class for all sympy objects, this single change should be inherited and fix the issue globally. We don't need to change `__ne__` because it is already implemented as `return not self.__eq__(other)` which will handle the negation of the result.

I think the root cause is that `reprec` and `imprec` are referenced before assignment in `evalf` when the real or imaginary part of the fallback evaluation (`xe.as_real_imag()`) is not a number and not zero (such as with symbolic expressions like `Max(0, y)`). We should initialize `reprec` and `imprec` to `None` at the beginning of the fallback block in `evalf` (near line 1290 in `sympy/core/evalf.py`) to avoid this `UnboundLocalError`.

I think the NameError is due to a missing definition of `cotm` in `coth.eval`. Since `coth` is related to `cot` for imaginary arguments, we should import `cot` from `sympy.functions.elementary.trigonometric` and define `cotm = cot(m)` in `sympy/functions/elementary/hyperbolic.py` before it is used in the check `if cotm is S.ComplexInfinity:`.

I think the root cause of the incorrect product evaluation for `Product(n + 1/2**k, [k, 0, n-1])` is in `_eval_product` in `sympy/concrete/products.py`. When handling `term.is_Add`, the code currently splits the numerator using `p.as_coeff_Add()` and sums the products of the split parts. However, `as_coeff_Add` returns a tuple `(coeff, rest)` which doesn't properly list all individual terms if there are multiple variables. We should change this to use `p.as_ordered_terms()` to iterate over all terms of the addition, so that the product of each term is computed and summed correctly.

I think the root cause is in `Interval._complement` in `sympy/sets/sets.py`. When the `other` set is a `FiniteSet` containing both symbols and numbers, we currently try to evaluate the complement by delegating to `Set._complement`. Instead, we should check if `other` has any symbols, and if it does, we should return the complement unevaluated as `Complement(other, self, evaluate=False)` to prevent incorrect evaluation of symbolic containment.

I think the root cause of the shift in `Matrix.col_insert` is that when we calculate the index for columns that are shifted after the insertion point, we are subtracting `other.cols` which shifts it too far left. In `sympy/matrices/common.py` inside `_eval_col_insert`, we should add `other.cols` instead of subtracting it to correctly offset the index relative to `pos`. Specifically, we should change `self[i, j - pos - other.cols]` to `self[i, j - pos + other.cols]`.

I think the root cause is that `Mul` object creation does not trigger polynomial multiplication when the polynomial is on the right side of the expression. We should modify `Mul.flatten` in `sympy/core/mul.py`. Specifically, we should check if any of the terms in the multiplication sequence `seq` has `is_Poly` set to `True`. If so, we should extract the `Poly` objects and the non-`Poly` objects, multiply the non-`Poly` objects together first, and then multiply the result with the `Poly` object by calling its `__rmul__` method. This will ensure that the multiplication evaluates to a `Poly` instead of remaining as a `Mul` expression.

I think we should update LatexPrinter.__init__ in sympy/printing/latex.py to allow arbitrary string values for mul_symbol by using dict.get with a fallback to the symbol itself. Currently, it lookups the symbol in mul_symbol_table which restricts it to the predefined keys. By using get, we can support any custom latex symbol provided by the user.

We should change the initialization to:
```python
        self._settings['mul_symbol_latex'] = \
            mul_symbol_table.get(self._settings['mul_symbol'], self._settings['mul_symbol'])

        self._settings['mul_symbol_latex_numbers'] = \
            mul_symbol_table.get(self._settings['mul_symbol'] or 'dot', self._settings['mul_symbol'])
```
This is backwards-compatible and directly supports arbitrary symbols like `\\,`.

I think the best way to handle the evaluation of `polylog(2, 1/2)` and other special values is to implement them in `_eval_expand_func` rather than `eval`. This keeps the main `eval` method clean and avoids the overhead of checking these complex algebraic conditions every time a `polylog` object is created. For `polylog(1, z)`, the `exp_polar` is actually correct as it preserves branch cut information, so we should not remove it from the expansion. We should instead make sure the user calls `unpolarify` on the expanded expression if they want to simplify it.

I think the traceback `TypeError: Invalid NaN comparison` indicates that `cancel()` is encountering `NaN` values when processing the matrix entries during the Bareiss algorithm execution. Specifically, in `sympy/core/exprtools.py`, the function `factor_terms` tries to determine if terms are negative using `a.as_coeff_Mul()[0] < 0`, which fails when the coefficient is `NaN`. Since the Bareiss algorithm can produce intermediate `NaN` values when evaluating symbolic determinants that should simplify to zero, we should modify `factor_terms` to handle `NaN` coefficients gracefully. I think we should update the check in `sympy/core/exprtools.py` at line 1179 to check if the coefficient is not `NaN` before comparing: `if all(a.as_coeff_Mul()[0] is not S.NaN and a.as_coeff_Mul()[0] < 0 for a in list_args):`.

I think the root cause of these CDF evaluation errors and hangs is that the continuous distributions (such as `ArcsinDistribution`, `DagumDistribution`, `FrechetDistribution`, `KumaraswamyDistribution`, and others) do not define their support domain `set` property. By default, they inherit `set = Interval(-oo, oo)` from `SingleContinuousDistribution`. When we call `cdf`, it falls back to `compute_cdf` which integrates the PDF from `self.set.start` (which is `-oo`) to `x`. This causes the integration engine to fail, hang, or return incorrect values (for example, integrating Arcsin's PDF from `-oo` instead of its lower bound `a`). We should update these distribution classes to define their correct support `set` property (e.g., as a property returning `Interval(self.a, self.b)` for `ArcsinDistribution`, and `Interval(0, oo)` for distributions with positive support like `DagumDistribution` and `FrechetDistribution`). This will allow the integration engine in `compute_cdf` to work with the correct limits and successfully compute the CDFs without needing to manually define `_cdf` methods for every distribution.

I think the root cause is that `tensor_product_simp_Mul` does not handle `Pow` terms during simplification of multiplications. When we have a product of identical tensor products, like `tp(1,1)*tp(1,1)`, SymPy groups them into a `Pow` term. We should update `tensor_product_simp_Mul` to detect `Pow` terms in the multiplication, extract their bases and exponents, and simplify them within the multiplication helper.

I think the root cause is that `_print_MatAdd` in the printers (str, latex, pretty) doesn't format negative terms with a minus sign, unlike `_print_Add` which checks if a term's printed form starts with `'-'` and adjusts the join operator accordingly. We should update `_print_MatAdd` in `sympy/printing/str.py`, `sympy/printing/latex.py`, and `sympy/printing/pretty/pretty.py` to implement sign checking on the printed terms similar to `_print_Add`.

I think the root cause is that `_print_Relational` in `sympy/printing/str.py` uses implicit string conversion for its arguments, which defaults to standard settings. We should update `_print_Relational` to use `sstr` with the printer's settings for subexpressions, like `sstr(expr.lhs, **self._settings)` and `sstr(expr.rhs, **self._settings)`. This will ensure settings like `sympy_integers` are respected when printing relational expressions.

I think the root cause is that `0 * N.x` (and `Vector(0)`) is represented as a `Vector` with empty `args` (i.e., `Vector([])`). This causes issues during addition because it lacks reference frame information. We should update `Vector.__init__` to ensure that even a zero vector retains a default reference frame, for example by storing it as `[(Matrix([0, 0, 0]), None)]` when it is initialized with `0` or simplifies to zero. This will allow the addition to proceed with a valid structure.

I think the root cause is that `MpmathPrinter` doesn't implement `_print_Rational`, so it falls back to the default Python division string representation (e.g., `1/3`). We should implement `_print_Rational` in `MpmathPrinter` (in `sympy/printing/pycode.py`) by converting the `Rational` object to a SymPy `Float` first, and then printing it using the existing `_print_Float` method. This allows us to reuse the robust float formatting logic already present in `MpmathPrinter`.

I think the root cause is that rank-0 arrays (scalars) are initialized with an empty shape `()`, which leads to a loop size of 0. We should update `_handle_ndarray_creation_inputs` in `sympy/tensor/array/ndim_array.py` to default to a shape of `(1,)` for scalar inputs in the else block, so that they are correctly treated as having one element.

I think the root cause is that `Max` is missing from the `known_functions` dictionary in `sympy/printing/mathematica.py`. We should update `known_functions` by adding `"Max": [(lambda *x: True, "Max")]` so that the printer knows how to translate it to the Mathematica equivalent.

I think the issue is in `Quaternion.to_rotation_matrix()`. Looking at the code, `m12` and `m21` are identical: both are defined as `2*s*(q.c*q.d + q.b*q.a)`. This symmetry is incorrect for a rotation matrix. I think we should update `m21` to be `2*s*(q.c*q.d - q.b*q.a)` to fix the sign mismatch and ensure the matrix is correctly oriented.

I think the root cause is that `Mod` does not distribute over multiplication terms during evaluation. We should update the `Mul` case in `Mod.eval` to recursively apply `Mod` to all non-modulus arguments, i.e., changing `non_mod_l` to `[cls(x, q) for x in non_mod_l]`, and then reconstruct the term if this changed the arguments.

I think the root cause is that `MinMaxBase` explicitly raises a `ValueError` when no arguments are provided. We should update `MinMaxBase.__new__` in `sympy/functions/elementary/miscellaneous.py` to return `S.Infinity` when `args` is empty, as returning infinity is mathematically convenient for these functions.

I think the root cause is that `Add._eval_is_zero` fails to recognize the imaginary nature of unexpanded terms like `(1 + I)**2`. We should update `_eval_is_zero` in `sympy/core/add.py` to expand each argument in `self.args` before performing the `is_real` and `is_imaginary` checks in the loop.

I think the root cause is that the MathML presentation printer incorrectly attempts to split symbols that end with numbers (like `x2`) into a base and a subscript (e.g. `x` and `2`), and then wraps them in a subscript tag (`msub`). This subscript representation is what Safari fails to render. I think we should update `_print_Symbol` in `sympy/printing/mathml.py` to check if a symbol ends with a digit using `sym.name[-1].isdigit()`. If it does, we should treat it as a single unit and print it directly as an identifier (`mi`) without splitting it, which will make it visible in Safari.

I think the root cause is that `posify` does not pass the `finite` assumption when creating the dummy replacement symbols. We should modify `posify` to check if the original symbol has `is_finite` set, and if so, pass `finite=s.is_finite` to the `Dummy` constructor. We can do this by updating `reps` definition to: `reps = {s: Dummy(s.name, positive=True, finite=s.is_finite) for s in eq.free_symbols if s.is_positive is None}`. This will ensure that the finiteness is preserved.

I think the root cause is that the assumptions system doesn't propagate the `integer` assumption to `finite`. Since even numbers are integers, and integers are finite, we should update `_assume_rules` in `sympy/core/assumptions.py` to include `integer -> finite`. We should also update `get_known_facts` in `sympy/assumptions/ask.py` to include `Implies(Q.integer, Q.finite)` to make sure the new assumptions system also inherits this behavior. This should fix the issue where `Symbol('m', even=True).is_finite` returns `None`.

I think the root cause is that `lambdify` relies on `LambdaPrinter` for converting SymPy expressions to Python code. We should implement the `_print_Indexed` method in `LambdaPrinter` within `sympy/printing/lambdarepr.py` to handle `Indexed` objects, formatting them as standard Python array indexing.

I think the issue is in how the Cython backend wrapper handles arguments that are not present in the wrapped expression. In `sympy/utilities/autowrap.py`, the `CythonCodeWrapper` partitions arguments and generates prototypes based on whether they have dimensions. When a `MatrixSymbol` is unused, it is passed without dimensions. We should update `CythonCodeWrapper._prototype_arg` and `CythonCodeWrapper._call_arg` to check if the argument is a `MatrixSymbol` and, if so, treat it as a numpy array using its shape, ensuring the Cython wrapper correctly passes it as a pointer.

I think the root cause is that `encode_morse` doesn't handle the conversion of the digit '1' correctly during the initial translation phase. We should use the `translate` function from `sympy.utilities.misc` to pre-process the message and map the character '1' to its correct Morse representation '.----' before entering the encoding loop. We can achieve this by adding `msg = translate(msg, {'1': '.----'})` at the beginning of `encode_morse`.

I think the root cause is that the helper function `_f` in `_TR56` (within `sympy/simplify/fu.py`) does not handle the case where the exponent is the imaginary unit `I`. When it attempts to check if `rv.exp < 0`, it raises a `TypeError` because complex numbers cannot be compared. We should add a check `if rv.exp == I: return rv` at the beginning of `_f` to safely bypass simplification for this case.

I think the root cause of the IndexError is that split_surds in radsimp.py assumes the expression always contains terms with square roots, which are extracted into the surds list. When the expression contains no such terms (for example, if it contains I which is not treated as a power), the surds list is empty, leading to _split_gcd failing when accessing the first element. Since sqrtdenest uses SqrtdenestStopIteration to signal that an expression cannot be denested, we should update split_surds to raise SqrtdenestStopIteration when surds is empty. This will terminate the denesting process and return the expression unchanged.

I think the root cause of the AttributeError during block matrix multiplication is that `BlockMatrix._blockmul` fails when the resulting blocks contain scalar `Zero` elements instead of `ZeroMatrix` objects, which triggers a `ValueError` in the `BlockMatrix` constructor. To make block multiplication more robust, we should add a try-except block in `BlockMatrix._blockmul` around the construction of the new `BlockMatrix`. If it fails with `ValueError` or `AttributeError`, we should fall back and return the symbolic multiplication `self * other`.

I think the root cause of the GeometryError is that `Point.__new__` doesn't know how to handle `Mul` expressions (like `2.0*Point2D(1, 1)`) when they are passed as arguments. When we try to add `point1 + sympy.sympify(2.0) * point2`, the right-hand side evaluates to a `Mul` object. Then, `Point.__add__` attempts to normalize the dimensions by calling `Point(other, evaluate=False)`, which fails in `Point.__new__` because it expects a sequence of coordinates, not a `Mul` object. We should update `Point.__new__` to check if the input is a `Mul` expression, and if it contains a `Point` and a scalar, we should extract them, perform the multiplication, and initialize the new `Point` with the scaled coordinates.

I think the issue is in how the solution tuples are reordered when `syms` does not match the internal sorted variable list `var`. Currently, `dict_sym_index` maps from `syms` to indices, but the tuple reconstruction loops over `var`, which results in incorrect mapping and even KeyErrors if `syms` is a subset of `var`. We should change the reordering logic in `diophantine` to create `dict_var_index` mapping `var` to indices and then construct the tuples by looping over `syms` instead. This ensures correct positioning of values for the requested symbols. Specifically, we should change the return statement under `if syms != var` in `sympy/solvers/diophantine.py` to use `dict_var_index = dict(zip(var, range(len(var))))` and loop over `syms` instead of `var` in the list comprehension.

I think the root cause of the crash in `nthroot_mod` when `a % p == 0` is that `_nthroot_mod1` calls `discrete_log(p, s1, h)` with `s1 = 0` (since `s` is a multiple of `p`). Because `discrete_log` is mathematically undefined for target `0`, it correctly raises a `ValueError: Log does not exist`. We should handle this by wrapping the `discrete_log` call in `_nthroot_mod1` with a `try-except` block and returning `None` (or `[]` if `all_roots` is True) when `ValueError` is caught, as this indicates that no discrete log (and thus no root) can be found using this method.

I think the root cause is that `solvify` raises `NotImplementedError` when it encounters a `ConditionSet` in `sympy/solvers/solveset.py`. We should modify `solvify` to return the `ConditionSet` directly instead of raising this error, so that functions calling it can receive the unsolved set representation.

I think the root cause is that `_generic_factor_list` returns the factors individually even if they have the same multiplicity. We should fix this in `sqf_list` by post-processing its returned factors. We can group the factors by their exponent, and for each group, multiply their bases using `Mul` to combine them into a single square-free factor before returning.

I think the root cause is that the LaTeX printer doesn't know how to parenthesize `Subs` expressions when they are part of a multiplication. We should update `_needs_mul_brackets` in `sympy/printing/latex.py` to return `True` for `Subs` expressions when they are not the last term, similar to how we handle `Integral` or `Sum`.

I think the root cause of the dropped factor is in `dmp_sqf_part` within `sympy/polys/sqfreetools.py`. Currently, it computes the square-free part by differentiating only with respect to the first variable (typically `x`) using `dmp_diff(f, 1, u, K)`. This causes it to treat factors that do not contain `x` (such as `y-1`) as constants, which then get lost during the GCD computation. We should update `dmp_sqf_part` to differentiate with respect to the second variable instead, by importing `dmp_diff_in` from `sympy.polys.densetools` and calling `dmp_diff_in(f, 1, 1, u, K)` when `u > 0`.

I think we should update `sympy/printing/repr.py` by adding `_print_dict` and `_print_set` to `ReprPrinter`. Since we want the representation of the elements, we should use the builtin `repr()` function to convert the keys and values of the dict, and the elements of the set, to their string forms before joining them with commas and wrapping them in braces.

I think the root cause of the strange behavior in `ConditionSet.subs` is that when the condition evaluates to `True` after substitution, it reconstructs the `ConditionSet` using the substituted value `new` as the dummy variable. We should update `sympy/sets/conditionset.py` in `_eval_subs` to use `self.sym` instead of `new` when returning `ConditionSet(new, Contains(new, base), base)` if `cond is S.true`. This will ensure the dummy variable remains unchanged.

I think the root cause of the UnboundLocalError is that kernS tries to run its space-replacement workaround even when the input string doesn't contain any spaces. In these cases, the `kern` variable is never initialized, leading to the error. I think we should update `kernS` to check if there are any spaces in the input string first, and if not, bypass the workaround and call `sympify` directly.

I think the root cause is that `IdentityOperator` does not recognize `Dagger` instances during multiplication simplification. We should update `IdentityOperator.__mul__` in `sympy/physics/quantum/operator.py` to return `other` if it is an instance of `Dagger`, similar to how it handles `Operator`.

I think the IndexError in `minimal_blocks` is due to a wrong subset check when filtering non-minimal blocks. In `sympy/combinatorics/perm_groups.py`, around line 2199, we check if `rep.issubset(r)`. However, we want to check if the already discovered block `r` is a subset of the new block `rep` to determine if `r` is not minimal. We should change this check to `r.issubset(rep)` to correctly identify which blocks to remove.

I think the root cause of the issue is in the `uniq` function in `sympy/utilities/iterables.py`. The `partitions` function is designed to reuse the same dictionary object for performance, which is documented in its docstring. When `uniq` receives the generator from `partitions`, it encounters a `TypeError` because dictionaries are unhashable, and falls back to a list-based lookup. In this fallback path, it checks `if s not in result` and appends `s` to `result`. However, since `result` stores references to the same dictionary object that `partitions` mutates in-place, the lookup `s not in result` evaluates to `False` for all items after the first one, causing `uniq` to yield only one partition. We should modify `uniq` to store copies of mutable items in `result` in its fallback path, rather than modifying `partitions` to yield copies, to avoid performance regression.

I think the traceback in `terms_gcd` is due to `dmp_terms_gcd` calling `monomial_min` with an empty set of monomials, which occurs when the polynomial dictionary representation `F` is empty because all coefficients are zero but the polynomial itself was not stripped. We should modify `dmp_terms_gcd` in `sympy/polys/densebasic.py` to check if `F` is empty and return early with zero degrees, or update `monomial_min` in `sympy/polys/monomials.py` to handle empty arguments gracefully.

I think the root cause of the `AttributeError: 'Complement' object has no attribute 'equals'` is that `Relational._eval_simplify` assumes that the difference between the two sides of a relation (which is a `Complement` set in this case) behaves like an `Expr` and has an `equals` method. Since `Set` objects do not inherit from `Expr`, they lack this method. We should implement `equals` on the base `Set` class in `sympy/sets/sets.py` to return `self.is_empty` when compared to `0`, which is how `_eval_simplify` checks for equality after subtraction. This will allow relational simplification to work for sets without raising errors.

I think the root cause is that `Symbol` instances allow setting arbitrary attributes because they have a `__dict__`. To enforce immutability as in version 1.6.2, we should override `__setattr__` in the `Symbol` class in `sympy/core/symbol.py` to prevent setting any attributes other than `name`. This will make the instances immutable again.

I think the root cause is that `BooleanFalse` (representing `S.false`) doesn't handle comparison with `Float` zero. We should update the `__eq__` method in `Boolean` (or `BooleanAtom` in `sympy/logic/boolalg.py`) to return `True` when compared with `S(0.0)`. This would make the comparison consistent in both directions, matching Python's behavior where `False == 0.0` is `True`.

I think the root cause of the pretty printing issue is in `pretty_symbol` within `sympy/printing/pretty/pretty_symbology.py`. Currently, it calls `split_super_sub` before translating unicode Greek characters. Because `split_super_sub` uses a regex that only matches ASCII letters, it fails to split names like `ω0`. We should modify `pretty_symbol` to check if the symbol name starts with a Greek character and ends with digits, and manually split it into name and subscript before translation, rather than relying on `split_super_sub` for these cases.

I think the root cause is in how hyperbolic functions evaluate their reality assumption when they have Piecewise arguments. Specifically, in `sinh._eval_is_real` (and similarly for `cosh` and `tanh` in `sympy/functions/elementary/hyperbolic.py`), we compute `im % pi` which calls `Mod` under the hood. When the argument contains `Piecewise`, this `Mod` call triggers `gcd` which fails with `PolynomialError: Piecewise generators do not make sense`. We should update these `_eval_is_real` methods to check if the argument contains `Piecewise` and return `None` immediately, avoiding the modulo operation.

I think the root cause is that `FiniteSet` is being instantiated with a tuple `xis` instead of its unpacked elements. In `sympy/sets/handlers/intersection.py`, we should change `base_set -= FiniteSet(xis)` to `base_set -= FiniteSet(*xis)` so that the individual solutions are correctly excluded from the base set.

I think the root cause of the missing brackets is that the LaTeX parser generates an overly complex, unevaluated expression tree for nested fractions. In `sympy/parsing/latex/_parse_latex_antlr.py`, the `convert_frac` function uses `evaluate=False` when constructing `Pow` and `Mul` objects. This prevents SymPy from simplifying `1/(1/c^2)` to `c^2`. We should remove `evaluate=False` in `convert_frac` to allow SymPy to evaluate and simplify the fraction during parsing, which will print correctly without missing brackets.

I think the root cause is that `itermonomials` does not correctly handle the case when `min_degrees` is passed as an integer. When `min_degrees` is an integer, it should be broadcasted to a list of the same length as `variables` (similar to how `max_degrees` should be handled if it's also an integer) so that the subsequent logic can process it consistently as a sequence. We should update the input validation and preparation in `itermonomials` to convert both `max_degrees` and `min_degrees` to lists when they are integers.

I think the root cause of the double superscript rendering issue in LaTeX is that the LaTeX printer does not protect superscripts for non-Symbol bases when they are raised to a power. Instead of modifying individual operator classes in `secondquant.py`, we should update the generic LaTeX printer in `sympy/printing/latex.py`. Specifically, we should modify `_helper_print_standard_power` to always call `parenthesize_super(base)` regardless of whether `expr.base.is_Symbol` is true. This will generically fix the double superscript issue for any expression raised to a power, ensuring they are properly wrapped in braces.

I think the root cause is that the `Mod` class is missing a precedence definition in `sympy/printing/precedence.py`. We should add `"Mod": PRECEDENCE["Mul"]` to `PRECEDENCE_VALUES` in `sympy/printing/precedence.py` so that it is treated with the same precedence as multiplication, which matches Python's `%` operator. This should allow the printer to correctly identify when to parenthesize it.

I think the issue is that `String` doesn't support instantiation with empty arguments, which is required for `expr.func(*expr.args)` to work since `String` has empty `args`. We should define `defaults = {'text': ''}` in the `String` class so that `String()` can be called without arguments.

I think the root cause is that `im(a)` returns an unevaluated `im` object when `evaluate(False)` is active, which is truthy in Python. We should update the check in `sympy/geometry/point.py` to call `.doit()` on `im(a)` to force its evaluation before checking if it is non-zero.

I think the root cause is that the `Min` and `Max` SymPy functions are missing from the `_known_functions_math` dictionary in `sympy/printing/pycode.py`. Since they are standard mathematical functions, we should add them there so they are correctly printed with the `math.` prefix (e.g., `math.min` and `math.max`), matching how other functions like `sin` and `cos` are handled. We should update `_known_functions_math` in `sympy/printing/pycode.py` to include `'Min': 'min'` and `'Max': 'max'`.

I think the issue is in `sympy/utilities/lambdify.py` inside the `_recursive_to_string` function. For tuple arguments, we are manually reconstructing the tuple string using `left + ', '.join(...) + right`. We should instead leverage Python's built-in tuple string representation to ensure correct formatting (like trailing commas for single-element tuples). I think we should change the `tuple` case in `_recursive_to_string` to return `str(tuple(_recursive_to_string(doprint, e) for e in arg))`.

I think the root cause is that the `_hermite_normal_form` function is only processing `min(m, n)` rows from the bottom. For matrices with more rows than columns ($m > n$), we are missing the top rows which might contain pivots. We should change `rows = min(m, n)` to `rows = max(m, n)` in `sympy/polys/matrices/normalforms.py` to ensure all rows are processed.

I think the root cause is that `UndefinedFunction` in `sympy/core/function.py` does not support sequence-like names when instantiated. When we call `symbols` with a nested tuple and `cls=Function`, it attempts to instantiate `UndefinedFunction` with these nested structures. We should update `UndefinedFunction.__new__` to detect if the `name` argument is a tuple or list, and if so, recursively create and return a tuple of `UndefinedFunction` instances.

I think the root cause is that the leading matrices insertion makes the final indices in `resulting_indices` end up completely reversed. We should update `kahane_simplify()` to reverse the order of the indices in `resulting_indices` at the very end of the function, just before we build the final `resulting_expr`.

I think the root cause of the AttributeError in Piecewise is that Contains is treated as a set-like object in some paths but lacks the necessary interface. We should update Contains.as_set in sympy/sets/contains.py to return self instead of raising NotImplementedError, and implement as_relational on the Contains class to return self. This satisfies the interface contract expected by Piecewise (i.e., c.as_set().as_relational(x)) by allowing Contains to act as its own set representation and relation.

I think the root cause is that the `Dimension` class does not automatically simplify compound dimensions that are equivalent to a dimensionless state. We should update `Dimension.__new__` to resolve the dimension's dependencies against the default SI dimension system (using `DimensionSystem.is_dimensionless`) and return `Dimension(1)` if it is dimensionless. This will ensure that `exp(expr)` correctly receives `Dimension(1)` as its argument dimension.

I think the root cause is that `_collect_factor_and_dimension` in `sympy/physics/units/unitsystem.py` uses `expr.scale_factor` and `expr.dimension` for `Quantity` objects, which resolves dimensions using the default unit system (SI) rather than the current system `self`. This leads to mismatches when resolving derived dimensions of quantities defined in custom or extended systems. We should update `_collect_factor_and_dimension` to use `self.get_quantity_scale_factor(expr)` and `self.get_quantity_dimension(expr)` to correctly resolve dimensions using the active unit system.

I think the root cause of the homomorphism check failure is that in `_check_homomorphism`, when trying to map presentation generators to domain generators for PermutationGroups, we are using `gens.index(r[i])`. Here, `gens` refers to the presentation generators (`domain.presentation().generators`), but we actually want the index in the domain's own generators. We should update this to use `domain.generators.index(r[i])` instead to get the correct generator mapping.

I think the root cause is that `PolyElement.as_expr` does not normalize the input symbols to ensure they are proper SymPy Symbol instances. We should modify `as_expr` in `sympy/polys/rings.py` to convert the incoming `symbols` arguments using the `Symbol` constructor, like `symbols = [Symbol(s) for s in symbols]` if they are provided, before passing them to `expr_from_dict`.

I think the root cause is that the `Rational` constructor doesn't properly parse decimal strings when a denominator is also provided as a string. We should check if the arguments are strings and convert them to `Float` first, then calculate the rational value of their division, to ensure that decimal values like '0.5' are correctly interpreted before we do the rational math.

I think we should resolve this by adding a new token transformation function, `convert_relationals`, in `sympy/parsing/sympy_parser.py`. This function should detect relational operators like `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `==` and convert them into their corresponding SymPy class calls (e.g., converting `A < B` to `Lt(A, B)`) at the token level, similar to how `convert_equals_signs` works for `Eq`. We should then add `convert_relationals` to `standard_transformations` so it is applied automatically.

I think for `User.existsBySlug`, when we pass an array of slugs, it should return a single boolean indicating if all of them exist, rather than returning an array of booleans. This makes it much cleaner to check for bulk existence in a single conditional statement, and we can then just return that single result.

I think we should implement `db.mget` in MongoDB by using a simple `{ _key: { $in: keys } }` query on the objects collection and mapping the returned documents to their data values, as MongoDB will handle the batch retrieval. For the email validation rate limiting, I think the best approach is to simplify `UserEmail.canSendValidation` so that it always returns `false` if `isValidationPending` is true. This will prevent users from triggering multiple confirmation emails while one is active, without needing to perform complex TTL calculations.

I think we should implement the 'old' sort mode by reusing the existing 'recent' database queries (since 'old' is just the reverse of 'recent' and we don't have 'topics:old' sets in the database) and then reversing the retrieved topic IDs in memory. Specifically, we should update `getTids`, `getTagTids`, and `getCidTids` in `src/topics/sorted.js` to treat `params.sort === 'old'` the same as `recent` when selecting the database sets (e.g., using `topics:recent` and `cid:${cid}:tids`). Then in `sortTids`, if `params.sort === 'old'`, we can just sort the results in memory by `lastposttime` ascending using a new comparator. This is much simpler than changing the database query methods to ascending versions, which might not be supported consistently across all database backends.

I think we should simplify the email validation pending check and prevent redundant emails. First, `UserEmail.isValidationPending` only needs to check if the database key `confirm:byUid:<uid>` exists and is not expired; we don't need to load the confirmation object and compare the email address because a user should only have one active validation flow at a time. Second, to prevent spamming users, `UserEmail.sendValidationEmail` should check if the user's email is already confirmed (by checking if the `email:confirmed` field is `1` on the user object) and throw an error if so, as there is no need to send validation emails to already verified accounts.

I think we should handle the merged topic resolution dynamically when accepting the post from the queue, rather than updating all queued posts during the merge process. Updating all queued posts eagerly during merge adds unnecessary database writes, especially since many queued posts might eventually be rejected. When `Posts.submitFromQueue` is called, we should check if the target topic has been deleted and merged into another topic by checking its `mergeIntoTid` field, and then update the `tid` on the fly before submitting the reply. We should look into `src/posts/queue.js` and modify `submitFromQueue` to perform this check.

I think we should enforce the system tag restriction directly during the topic creation and editing processes. Specifically, we should add validation logic in `src/topics/create.js` (inside `Topics.post`) and in `src/posts/edit.js` (inside the editing handler). We can fetch the configured system tags from `meta.config.systemTags` and, if the current user (using `user.isPrivileged(uid)`) is not privileged, prevent them from using these tags by throwing the `[[error:cant-use-system-tag]]` error. This directly targets the entry points where users try to save their tags, rather than messing with the internal helper functions.

I think we can resolve the thumbnail cleanup issue by implementing a new `Thumbs.deleteAll` method in `src/topics/thumbs.js` that retrieves all thumbnails for a topic and deletes them sequentially by calling the existing `Thumbs.delete` method in a loop. Then we just need to call this `Thumbs.deleteAll` during the topic purge process in `src/topics/delete.js`. This reuse of `Thumbs.delete` keeps the codebase clean and avoids modifying its signature to handle arrays, which is safer for backward compatibility.

I think we should implement the new HTTP invitation endpoints by reusing the existing socket handlers in `src/socket.io/groups.js` (such as `issueInvite`, `acceptInvite`, and `rejectInvite`) rather than writing new business logic in `src/api/groups.js` or deleting the socket handlers. The new express controllers in `src/controllers/write/groups.js` can import `src/socket.io/groups` and invoke those methods directly by passing the request parameters. This avoids code duplication and ensures that we maintain backwards compatibility for any external clients still relying on the socket interface. Specifically, we should route the new API endpoints directly to these existing socket handlers.

I think the root cause of duplicate topics during concurrent requests is that `User.isReadyToPost` in `src/user/posts.js` only checks the `lastposttime` but doesn't update it immediately. By the time the first request completes and updates `lastposttime` in `User.onNewPostMade`, other concurrent requests have already passed the `isReadyToPost` check. We should update `isReady` in `src/user/posts.js` to set the `lastposttime` (or `lastqueuetime` depending on the field) to the current time immediately after the validation checks pass, preventing concurrent requests from passing the check.

I think we should make `cleanOrphans` more robust by defaulting `orphanExpiryDays` to 30 if it is not configured in `meta.config`. This will ensure that the cleanup still runs with a safe default even if the admin hasn't set it up yet, and makes it easier to test the method without having to mock the config every time.

I think the root cause of the inconsistent ordering is that we are updating the sorted set with low scores (0, 1, 2...) which conflict with the timestamp-based scores (`Date.now()`) assigned when topics are initially pinned. This causes custom-ordered topics to get pushed to the bottom of the list. We should keep the client sending the array of all pinned topics and update the server to re-score them using a timestamp-based baseline (e.g. `Date.now() - index * 1000`) so that they maintain their correct relative order without being overridden by newer pins.

I think the root cause is that `helpers.valueToString` is converting the input array into a comma-separated string (e.g. `['b', 'd']` becomes `'b,d'`), which prevents the database drivers from processing them as multiple elements. We should bypass this conversion if the input is already an array, and pass the array directly to the database operations (like MongoDB's `$pull`, Redis's `lrem`, and PostgreSQL's `array_remove`), as they should support array arguments natively.

I think the best way to check if a user is allowed to access the forum during maintenance mode is to retrieve all the groups they belong to and compare them with the exempt groups list. We should update `src/middleware/maintenance.js` to retrieve the current user's groups using `groups.getUserGroups([req.uid])`. Then, we can check if there is any intersection between these groups and the `groupsExemptFromMaintenanceMode` from the configuration. This approach is cleaner and more efficient than making multiple individual membership checks for each exempt group.

I think we should update `db.getObject` and `db.getObjects` in the database backends to support the `fields` parameter by delegating to `getObjectFields` and `getObjectsFields` respectively. Additionally, to optimize the response and avoid sending unnecessary data, we should filter the results to remove any fields that are `null` or `undefined` before returning them. This will ensure we only return clean objects containing actual data.

I think that for security and privacy reasons, we should not return `[[error:invalid-data]]` when required identifiers (like `roomId`, `mid`, or `uid`) are missing or invalid in the chats and users API. Doing so can leak information about whether a room or message exists. Instead, we should consistently return `[[error:no-privileges]]` for these validation failures, matching the behavior of unauthorized access. This will prevent potential enumeration attacks.

I think the best way to handle the authorization for the new `webfinger` endpoint is to reuse the existing `middleware.canViewUsers` route middleware. This ensures we adhere to the global `view:users` privilege configuration. We should mount it in `src/routes/well-known.js` like `app.get('/.well-known/webfinger', middleware.canViewUsers, controllers['well-known'].webfinger);`. This way, we don't need to manually check privileges inside the controller itself, keeping the controller logic clean.

I think we should avoid database migrations and potential compatibility issues by keeping the stored upload paths in the database without the 'files/' prefix. We can resolve the path inconsistency by updating `src/posts/uploads.js` to dynamically add the 'files/' prefix if it's missing when resolving files on disk, and similarly strip it when performing database operations. This will ensure that we don't break existing data while still allowing the uploads to be located correctly on disk.

I think we should implement `sortedSetIncrByBulk` in a database-agnostic way by retrieving the current scores of the members first, calculating the updated scores in memory, and then applying the updates using `sortedSetAddBulk`. This approach avoids writing database-specific bulk increment logic for each adapter (especially Postgres, where concurrent individual updates can lead to deadlocks) and ensures a consistent interface across Redis, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL by reusing the existing bulk write mechanisms.

I think we should ensure that the `min` and `max` parameters are strictly numeric before they reach the database queries to prevent syntax errors or potential query issues, especially in Postgres and Mongo. We should parse them using `parseFloat()` within each database's `sortedSetsCardSum` implementation, defaulting `min` to `0` and `max` to a very large number if they are not provided or if parsing fails.

I think we can implement `incrObjectFieldByBulk` by reusing the existing `incrObjectFieldBy` method to avoid duplicating the database-specific increment logic, caching, and validation. In `src/database/mongo/hash.js` and `src/database/redis/hash.js`, we should just loop through the input `data` array and, for each key-value pair, iterate over the fields to call `module.incrObjectFieldBy(key, field, value)` in parallel using `Promise.all`. This keeps the implementation clean and consistent across all database backends.

I think we should validate the plugin ID in the socket handler `src/socket.io/admin/plugins.js` inside `Plugins.toggleActive`. Since the admin panel triggers plugin activation via WebSockets, validating the `plugin_id` there using `pluginNamePattern` from `src/constants.js` will prevent invalid IDs from being processed and allow us to return the `[[error:invalid-plugin-id]]` error to the user before any core state changes are attempted.

I think we should optimize the token retrieval process. Since `lastSeen` is updated frequently and stored in a separate sorted set (`tokens:lastSeen`), we should keep it separate from the static token metadata stored in `token:{token}`. When calling `utils.tokens.get` or `utils.tokens.list`, we should only retrieve the static metadata (`uid`, `description`, `timestamp`) to keep the operation lightweight and fast. Callers who actually need the `lastSeen` timestamps (such as the admin control panel) should invoke `utils.tokens.getLastSeen` separately rather than having `get` merge it automatically.

I think we should implement `User.getLocalCoverPath` and `User.getLocalAvatarPath` in `src/user/picture.js` by checking the filesystem directly rather than relying on database fields which might be out of sync. We can loop through the extensions returned by `User.getAllowedProfileImageExtensions()` to construct the expected file paths (e.g., `path.join(nconf.get('upload_path'), 'profile', "${uid}-profilecover.${ext}")`) and use `fs.access` to check if they exist. Once these utility functions are implemented, we should use them in `User.removeCoverPicture` and `User.removeProfileImage` to identify the file to delete, and also update `deleteImages` in `src/user/delete.js` to use them for cleaning up files during account deletion.

I think the root cause is that `SocketPosts.getUpvoters` does not check category read permissions for the requesting user. To resolve this, we should fetch the category IDs of the posts using `posts.getCidsByPids` and then verify the user's category-level access. We can check if the user is allowed to read the categories by calling `privileges.categories.isUserAllowedTo('read', ...)` with the category IDs. If the user lacks `read` privilege on any of the category IDs, we should throw a `[[error:no-privileges]]` error.

I think we should implement the file deletion logic in a new method `Posts.uploads.deleteFromDisk` in `src/posts/uploads.js`. To ensure safety and prevent deleting files that are still referenced by other posts, `deleteFromDisk` should check if each file is an orphan using `Posts.uploads.isOrphan` before unlinking it. Additionally, since the purge process always handles lists of uploads retrieved from the database, we can assume the inputs are safe and always formatted as arrays, so we don't need to add path traversal checks or support single string inputs in `deleteFromDisk`.

I think the root cause is that `Topics.updateTopicTags` overwrites all tags on the topic, causing system tags to be lost if they aren't included in the edit request. We should modify `Topics.updateTopicTags` in `src/topics/tags.js` to fetch the current tags first, identify any system tags, and merge them back into the new tags list before calling `createTags`.

I think we need to ensure the error message from `validateUpload` is correctly formatted on the server side to match the security requirements. Specifically, the allowed MIME types list in the `invalid-image-type` error must be joined by `&#44;` and all forward slashes (`/`) must be encoded as `/` before throwing the error. We should implement this formatting in `validateUpload` so that the server responds with the fully encoded error message.

I think the root cause of the private fields leak is that the low-level data retrieval function `User.getUsersFields` in `src/user/data.js` does not enforce privacy filtering. We should update `User.getUsersFields` to accept an optional `callerUID` parameter, and if it is not provided (or if the caller lacks privileges), we should filter out the `email` and `fullname` fields according to user and global settings. This will secure all endpoints that retrieve user data, not just the write API, by ensuring the data is filtered at the database retrieval level.

I think we can fix the resend inconsistency by checking the remaining lifetime of the confirmation. We should update `UserEmail.canSendValidation` to check if the remaining TTL returned by `UserEmail.getValidationExpiry` is less than the configured `emailConfirmInterval` in milliseconds. If it is, then the cooldown has passed and we can safely allow the resend; otherwise, we should block it.

I think we can simplify the implementation by storing the allow and deny lists as JSON-serialized strings in the user settings hash (just like other settings), and then directly using JavaScript's `.includes()` method on `settings.chatAllowList` and `settings.chatDenyList` in `src/messaging/index.js`. Since these settings are loaded as strings from the database, we don't need to add a custom JSON parser in `src/user/settings.js` to convert them to arrays, which keeps our changes minimal and avoids modifying the core settings loading logic.

I think the root cause of the issue is that we are currently enforcing email presence during invitation verification because our database is keyed by email (`invitation:email:${email}`). To support token-only registration without requiring a complex database migration for existing invitations, we should keep the database schema as is. Instead, we can implement a helper function on the backend to retrieve the invited email by scanning the invitation records when only a token is provided. We should update `User.verifyInvitation` to make the `email` parameter optional, and if it's not provided, use this new lookup helper to find the email associated with the token before performing the validation. We should also update `User.joinGroupsFromInvitation` and `User.deleteInvitationKey` to resolve the email from the token using the same lookup helper if needed.

I think modifying the existing `sortedSetsCardSum` function to accept `min` and `max` parameters is risky as it is used in multiple places like `src/topics/tags.js` and `src/controllers/accounts/posts.js` which might expect the original behavior. We should instead implement a new method `sortedSetsCardSumByScore` in each database adapter to handle range-based counting, and then update `src/controllers/accounts/helpers.js` to call this new method. This avoids modifying the signature of `sortedSetsCardSum` and minimizes risk of breaking other features.

I think the root cause of the inconsistent blocking is that we are trying to register `chat:privileged` as a standard global privilege in `_privilegeMap` inside `src/privileges/global.js`. Doing so automatically exposes it to helper functions like `userPrivileges` and `groupPrivileges`, which are used by categories and will cause unintended side effects. Instead, we should implement the `chat:privileged` check dynamically inside `privileges.global.can` without adding it to `_privilegeMap`, and handle the UI rendering separately. This keeps the privilege system clean and avoids bloating the category privilege sets.

I think we can simplify the implementation by reusing the existing `User.getUidsByUsernames` function instead of creating a new `User.getUidsByUserslugs` helper. Since we are already slugifying the input in `meta.userOrGroupExists`, we can just pass the array of slugs to `User.getUidsByUsernames` in `User.existsBySlug` to get the corresponding UIDs and check their existence.

I think the root cause is that the `registrationComplete` middleware is blocking the `/confirm/` route because it's not in the allowed list. We should update the allowed list in `src/middleware/user.js` to include `/confirm/` (using a prefix check to match the code). This will allow the confirmation link to go through.

I think we should implement the backlink synchronization in `src/topics/posts.js` with a few specific behaviors. First, we should only parse absolute URLs that match the site's base URL from `nconf.get('url')` using a standard URL parser, as the composer formats these before saving and we don't need to support bare `/topic/{tid}` paths. Second, when a post is edited and a link is removed, we should clean up the database by also deleting the corresponding `backlink` event from the referenced topic's events so we don't leave stale timeline events. Finally, we should allow self-references within the same topic since linking to previous posts in the same thread is common and useful for navigation.

I think the root cause is that the custom avatar background color is not being persisted correctly. We should update `src/socket.io/user/picture.js` to save the selected `bgColor` to the user's fields as `icon:bgColor`. Then, in `src/user/data.js`, we can add `icon:bgColor` to the `fieldAllowlist` so it gets loaded. In `modifyUserData`, we can check if `user['icon:bgColor']` is present and use it, otherwise fall back to the default hashed color. We should keep the `user.hasOwnProperty('picture')` check as is to ensure we only process this when the picture field is present in the user data.

I think the root cause is that WebFinger is trying to resolve the instance actor, but the application actor's `preferredUsername` is not correctly aligned with the forum's domain. We should update the application actor in `src/controllers/activitypub/actors.js` to use `nconf.get('url_parsed').host` as its `preferredUsername`. Then, in `src/controllers/well-known.js`, we should check if the WebFinger resource slug matches this same `host` value to return the instance actor.

I think the root cause of the failure in `deleteObjectFields` is that we are not ensuring the `key` is a string before passing it to Redis, which can cause issues if it's passed in different formats. Also, the early return check `!fields.length` is redundant because the Redis driver should be able to handle empty arrays gracefully. We should update `src/database/redis/hash.js` to convert `key` to a string at the start of `deleteObjectFields` and remove the `!fields.length` check to simplify the logic.

I think we can implement `getSortedSetMembersWithScores` and `getSortedSetsMembersWithScores` by leveraging the existing `getSortedSetRangeWithScores` database helper. If you look at the implementations in `src/database/redis/sorted.js`, `mongo/sorted.js`, and `postgres/sorted.js`, `getSortedSetRangeWithScores` is already fully implemented, handles both single keys and arrays of keys (using `ANY` in Postgres, `$in` in MongoDB, and batching in Redis), and correctly returns `{ value, score }` objects. We should update these files to simply wrap `getSortedSetRangeWithScores(key, 0, -1)` and `getSortedSetRangeWithScores(keys, 0, -1)` to avoid duplicating database query logic.

I think we should avoid modifying the shared helper `spawnPrivilegeStates` in `public/src/modules/helpers.common.js` to add `data-type` to cells. Changing the helper's signature and modifying the templates (`category.tpl`, `global.tpl`) is risky and can be avoided. Instead, we can implement the filtering logic in `public/src/admin/manage/privileges.js` by dynamically determining the column indices to toggle based on the `labelData` returned from the API. We can map the filter to the active privilege indices and toggle the corresponding `th`/`td` elements by their column index. This achieves the same filtering behavior without altering the DOM structure of the cells.

I think we should reuse the existing `postsAPI.get` method to implement the new Write API endpoints for retrieving raw post content and summaries. `postsAPI.get` is already well-tested, handles all the necessary read privilege checks, and correctly manages deleted posts by returning a standard placeholder. We can update `src/controllers/write/posts.js` to call `postsAPI.get` and then extract the `content` for the raw endpoint, and return the post object directly for the summary endpoint. This will prevent code duplication and ensure we use the established security controls.

I think we should move the message content validation and the `canEdit` authorization checks from the core messaging library and socket modules into the new `Chats.messages.edit` controller. Since we are deprecating the socket-based edit path (`SocketModules.chats.edit`) in favor of the new PUT API route, we should centralize this logic in the HTTP controller to avoid duplication and keep the model layer focused purely on database operations. We can remove the `canEdit` check from `SocketModules.chats.edit` and `checkContent` from `Messaging.editMessage` to simplify them before their eventual removal.

I think the root cause is that the file upload controller in `src/controllers/uploads.js` does not verify if the target directory exists before saving the file. We should update `uploadsController.uploadFile` in `src/controllers/uploads.js` to check if the destination directory exists (using `file.exists` or `fs.promises.stat`) before calling `saveFileToLocal`, and return a `[[error:invalid-path]]` error if it is missing.

I think the root cause is that `VarsWithSources` is a custom mapping class but does not implement the union operator `__or__`. When `combine_vars` attempts `a | b` in replace mode, it fails because `VarsWithSources` does not support the `|` operator. We should implement the `__or__` method in `VarsWithSources` in `lib/ansible/vars/manager.py` to return a merged dictionary of its data and the other mapping.

I think the root cause is that the encryption utility in `lib/ansible/utils/encrypt.py` does not correctly handle salt values that contain embedded parameters like `ident`. When `_hash` is called, it passes the raw salt string (which may include `ident=...` from the file) directly to the passlib library, causing value errors. We should update `_hash` in `lib/ansible/utils/encrypt.py` to parse and strip any embedded `ident` from the `salt` parameter before passing it to the hashing algorithm, and ensure that if an `ident` is found in the salt, it is used as the `ident` setting.
