We should update `_parse_value` to accept a `max_val` parameter (defaulting to 255.0) and use it for normalization. When parsing HSV or HSVA colors in `to_py`, we should pass 359.0 as the `max_val` to `_parse_value` for all components so that they are scaled correctly relative to the HSV color space.

I think we should implement the `SelectionReason` enum using `enum.auto()` for its values to avoid hardcoding strings. Since the selection reasons are only used internally for tracking and debugging, using auto-incremented integer values is cleaner and more maintainable. We should also update `SelectionInfo.__str__` to use `self.reason.value` to print this identifier.

I think the root cause of the missing suggestions is in `CommandParser.parse`. We should implement the command suggestion logic there using `difflib.get_close_matches` when we handle `KeyError` for unknown commands. For empty inputs, we should introduce the `EmptyCommandError` class as a subclass of `NoSuchCommandError` and raise it in `CommandParser.parse` when `cmdstr` is empty. The `_parse_all_gen` method doesn't need to be updated because it's just a wrapper and `parse` is the main entry point where the command actually gets parsed and validated.

I think the root cause is that `interpolate_color` needs to be relocated to `qutebrowser/utils/qtutils.py` because it is Qt-dependent. When doing so, we should simplify the implementation by removing the legacy `_get_color_percentage` helper and instead performing direct inline interpolation of the color channels. Additionally, since the progress indicators in `downloads.py` and `tabbedbrowser.py` always pass a valid colorspace, we can safely remove the support for `colorspace=None` to clean up the code.

I think the root cause of the TypeError is that PyQt5 has trouble with integer coercion when wrapping QWebEnginePage.FindFlags. To fix this cleanly, we should implement the `_FindFlags` dataclass to store the logical state. For `to_qt()`, we should have it return the raw integer value of the combined flags (e.g. by using bitwise OR on the integer values of the enums) to avoid passing complex Qt enum types back to PyQt. For `__str__()`, we should just return the names of the active fields (like 'case_sensitive' or 'backward') joined by '|' (or 'none' if empty) to keep the string representation simple and avoid hardcoding Qt-specific enum names in our internal logs. Finally, in `prev_result`, we can just temporarily toggle the `backward` attribute of `self._flags` before calling `_find` and then toggle it back, which avoids the overhead of copying the flags object.

I think we should add the 1-hour cleanup timer to `GUIProcess` for successful processes as requested, but when the timer fires, the cleanup should simply delete the PID key from the `all_processes` dictionary (for example, using `all_processes.pop(self.pid, None)`). This is a cleaner approach because if the key is completely removed, we do not need to modify `miscmodels.py` or `qutescheme.py` to handle or filter out `None` values, and it prevents the registry from accumulating empty keys over time.

I think we should use `mimetypes.guess_extension` instead of `mimetypes.guess_all_extensions` in the `extra_suffixes_workaround` method. Using `guess_all_extensions` will pull in too many uncommon or obsolete file extensions (like `.jpe` for JPEG images, or `.m1v` for MPEG videos) which will clutter the file selection dialog. We should stick to the single primary extension returned by `guess_extension` to keep the file chooser clean and user-friendly.

I think we can simplify the duration parsing in `parse_duration` by using `re.findall` to extract all the numeric values and their corresponding unit suffixes (h, m, s) instead of using a complex single regular expression. We can use a regex like `r'([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)([hms])'` to find all valid components. This allows us to easily support fractional values, ignore any whitespace, and handle any combination of hours, minutes, and seconds. If the input string is a plain integer (consisting only of digits), we can check this first using `isdigit()` and return it directly as milliseconds.

I think the root cause is that `GUIProcess` is configured to only read from the standard output channel during execution because we explicitly set `self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)` in `__init__`. To allow live streaming of both `stdout` and `stderr` without complicating the signal connections, we should set the process channel mode to `QProcess.MergedChannels`. This will redirect `stderr` into the standard output channel, allowing the existing `readyRead` signal and `_on_ready_read` slot to handle live output from both streams automatically.

I think we should modify the `qt_args` function in the new `qtargs.py` module to not prepend `sys.argv[0]` to the argument list. PyQt's `QApplication` constructor is capable of determining the executable name on its own, so passing it explicitly in the arguments list is redundant and might lead to duplicate arguments in some startup paths. We should start the `argv` list as an empty list instead.

I think the root cause of the incorrect handling of numbers in encoded characters is that we are performing regex matching on the raw URL string segments which may contain percent-encoded entities (like `%3A` matching the digit `3`). We should decode the URL segments using `urllib.parse.unquote` before applying the regular expression, perform the increment/decrement on the decoded value, and then re-encode the result using `urllib.parse.quote` before setting it back to the QUrl. This avoids having to write complex regex lookarounds.

I think the root cause is that `custom_headers` always retrieves the global `Accept-Language` header because it doesn't know if it's being called for an XHR request where we want to avoid the fallback. We should update `custom_headers` in `qutebrowser/browser/shared.py` to accept a new keyword-only argument `fallback_accept_language: bool = True` and pass it to `config.instance.get` as `fallback`. Then, in `qutebrowser/browser/webengine/interceptor.py`, we should update `interceptRequest` to pass `fallback_accept_language=not is_xhr` when calling `custom_headers`.

I think the root cause of the URL parsing issues is that we are not properly isolating search term parsing from URL validation. For the search engine base URL issue, `_get_search_url` is incorrectly overriding the URL because it checks if the search term matches a search engine name even when an explicit engine was already prefixed. We should fix this in `_get_search_url` by changing the condition to: `if config.val.url.open_base_url and engine is None and term in config.val.url.searchengines:`. For the naive URL validation failures like `example_search.string`, we should tighten the TLD check in `_is_url_naive` by verifying that the last component of the host is alphabetic using `host.split('.')[-1].isalpha()`. Additionally, we should reject inputs with literal spaces early in `is_url` if they don't start with a scheme like `http://` or `https://`.

I think the WebKit `CertificateErrorWrapper` constructor needs to be updated to accept the `reply` object so we can ignore SSL errors properly. To avoid breaking the existing unit tests in `tests/unit/browser/webkit/test_certificateerror.py` which don't have a reply object, we should make `reply` the first parameter but optional, like `def __init__(self, reply=None, errors=None)`. This way, the tests can continue to instantiate it with just the errors list, and we can update `networkmanager.py` to pass the reply.

I think we should refactor `BlocklistDownloads` to inherit from `QObject` and replace the callbacks with Qt signals. Specifically, we should define `single_download_finished` to emit both the source `QUrl` and the downloaded file object (i.e., `pyqtSignal(QUrl, object)`). This is important because it allows consumers to identify which specific blocklist URL completed, which is crucial for detailed logging and error handling. In `_download_blocklist_url`, we should use `functools.partial` to pass the `url` to `_on_download_finished` so it can be emitted. We should also add `all_downloads_finished` as a signal emitting the finished count.

I think the root cause is that unbound signals do not have the `signal` attribute, which causes the `AttributeError`. To fix this, we should check if the signal has a `signatures` attribute (which contains the signal's signatures as a tuple). If it does, we can extract the signal name by taking the first signature and removing the `'()'` characters. If it doesn't have `signatures`, we should fall back to the existing `sig.signal` parsing.

I think the issue with the wrong PID in the error message is because we are relying on the cached `self.pid` which might not be updated or could be cleared. To ensure we always display the correct and current PID, we should retrieve it directly from the QProcess object when the process finishes. We should update `GUIProcess._on_finished` to construct the message using `self._proc.processId()` instead of `self.pid`, like: `msg = f"{self.outcome} See :process {self._proc.processId()} for details."`.

I think we can simplify the refactoring by avoiding the introduction of a new `init` function in `qtlog.py`. We can just move `qt_message_handler` to `qutebrowser/utils/qtlog.py` and import the `_args` variable directly from `qutebrowser.utils.log` at the module level. This allows the handler to access `_args.debug` without needing to pass it through an initialization function, keeping the changes to `qutebrowser/utils/log.py` minimal.

I think the root cause is that we need to check the new `content.javascript.log_message.excludes` config. Since the keys of `excludes` and `levels` represent the source of the log message (which is usually a static string like `userscript:_qute_stylesheet` or `qute:bla`), we should look them up directly in the dictionaries for better performance and simplicity, instead of using glob matching on the keys. We only need to use glob matching for the values in `excludes` (the error messages themselves), since those are the ones that contain wildcard patterns like `*`. So in `_js_log_to_ui`, we should do direct key lookups like `message_levels.get(source)` and `message_excludes.get(source)`.

I think we should avoid changing the signature of `config.instance.dump_userconfig` to keep the API stable and prevent breaking changes. Instead, we should implement the hidden settings display by adding a new URL handler `qute://configdiff-hidden` in `qutebrowser/browser/qutescheme.py`. When this URL is loaded, we can access `config.instance._values` directly and dump the hidden settings. In `qutebrowser/config/configcommands.py`, we should update the `config_diff` command to load `qute://configdiff-hidden` if the `--include-hidden` flag is provided, and keep loading `qute://configdiff` otherwise. This avoids polluting the existing dump method and keeps the URL routing clean without needing query parameter parsing.

I think we should implement this workaround by setting the `QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS` environment variable in `qtargs.py`'s `init_envvars` function, rather than modifying `_qtwebengine_args` directly. This keeps the command-line argument generation clean and avoids altering how Chromium arguments are composed at runtime. We can use `QLocale.system().name()` to get the system locale, and if we are on Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3 and the workaround is enabled, we can append the appropriate `--lang=<fallback>` flag to `QTWEBENGINE_CHROMIUM_FLAGS`.

I think we should update `StateConfig._set_changed_attributes` in `qutebrowser/config/configfiles.py` to compare the old and new version segments directly. We can obtain the version objects using `utils.parse_version` and then compare their segments by index using the `segments()` method. Specifically, if index 0 differs, it is a `VersionChange.major` change; if index 0 is equal but index 1 differs, it is a `VersionChange.minor` change; and if index 0 and 1 are equal but index 2 differs, it is a `VersionChange.patch` change. If all segments are equal, it is `VersionChange.equal`.

I think the crash is caused by `modeparsers.py` trying to construct a `Qt.Key` from an unknown key code (`0`) when handling system events on Qt6/Wayland. We should update `modeparsers.py` to check if `e.key()` is `0` or `Qt.Key.Key_unknown` (if it exists) and return `QKeySequence.SequenceMatch.NoMatch` immediately, bypassing the `keyutils.is_special` check. This avoids passing invalid integers to `Qt.Key` and prevents the crash without needing to refactor the helper functions in `keyutils.py` into `KeyInfo` methods.

I think we can simplify the implementation of the `qt.workarounds.disable_accelerated_2d_canvas` setting by defining the `auto` behavior statically in `_WEBENGINE_SETTINGS` using `machinery.IS_QT6`, similar to how `qt.chromium.experimental_web_platform_features` is handled. This avoids the need to refactor `_qtwebengine_settings_args` to accept the `versions` object, keeping our changes minimal and localized.

I think we should simplify `hide_qt_warning` in `qutebrowser/utils/qtlog.py` by always applying the filter to the default `'qt'` logger. Since this utility is specifically designed for hiding Qt warnings, hardcoding it to the main `'qt'` logger simplifies the implementation and avoids having to dynamically look up and apply filters to different logger names passed as arguments.

I think the SQLite `user_version` is a standard 32-bit integer, so we should pack the major and minor versions by splitting the 32 bits equally: 16 bits for the major version and 16 bits for the minor version. This allows both major and minor versions to range from 0 to 65535 (0xFFFF). We can implement `from_int` to unpack using `major = num >> 16` and `minor = num & 0xFFFF`, and `to_int` to pack them back using `(major << 16) | minor`. We should validate that `num` is a valid 32-bit integer (up to 4294967295) and that `major` and `minor` are within the 0-65535 range.

I think we should focus on renaming the command from `buffer` to `tab-select` in `qutebrowser/browser/commands.py` and updating the default keybindings. The completion models `buffer` and `other_buffer` in `qutebrowser/completion/models/miscmodels.py` are internal APIs and don't need to be renamed, as they are not user-facing and renaming them might break third-party scripts or plugins that import them.

I think the issue is that we are using '6.2.3' as the lower bound in `webview.py`, but the comment and the Qt bug report indicate that versions strictly greater than '6.2.2' are affected. We should update the lower bound check to `qtutils.version_check("6.2.2")` in `webview.py` to properly include '6.2.3' and other micro releases, and we should keep the default `compiled=True` behavior to ensure we don't enable the workaround if the compiled PyQt version doesn't match the runtime capabilities.

I think the root cause is that `qurl_from_user_input` in `qutebrowser/utils/urlutils.py` does not correctly handle URL-encoded characters when constructing the final QUrl from the search template. Specifically, when `open_base_url` is enabled, QUrl's automatic parsing in `fromUserInput` might misinterpret the encoded search query if it contains hyphens or other special characters, leading to incorrect host resolution. We should modify `qurl_from_user_input` to properly handle pre-encoded parameters, or avoid using `QUrl.fromUserInput` for search URLs.

I think we can avoid changing the regex in `Font` and making invasive changes to `configtypes.py` by resolving the `default_size` and `default_family` tokens dynamically inside `configinit.py`. We should update `late_init` and `_update_font_defaults` to iterate over all font settings (e.g., of type `Font` or `QtFont`). If their current value contains the tokens `default_size` or `default_family`, we can perform string replacement on their values with the configured default size and family, and then call `config.instance.set_obj` to update the config with the resolved string. This keeps the token resolution logic centralized in the configuration initialization rather than spreading it across multiple types and modifying the validation regex.

I think we should reuse the existing `ProgressTracker` class instead of creating a new `OperationProgressTracker` to track the import progress. `ProgressTracker` is already designed to manage multiple progress monitors via `registerMonitor` and `workDoneForMonitor`. We can register a monitor for the calendar import, and then update it from `CalendarFacade` by calling `this.worker.getMainInterface().progressTracker.workDoneForMonitor(monitorId, progress)`. In the UI, we can observe the progress through the existing progress tracker.

I think we can support vCard 4.0 imports quickly and safely by preprocessing the input in `vCardFileToVCards` to replace `VERSION:4.0` with `VERSION:3.0` before validation. Since the fields we care about are mapped the same way as vCard 3.0, this allows us to reuse the existing parsing path without modifying the complex version checks. For the email fields, we should add explicit case statements for `ITEM3.EMAIL` and `ITEM4.EMAIL` in `vCardListToContacts` to handle modern Apple and ProtonMail exports, keeping the switch block simple.

I think we should implement `PriceAndConfigProvider` as a singleton to avoid fetching the configuration and pricing data multiple times from the network and service executor. We can add a private static `instance` field and return it in `PriceAndConfigProvider.getInitializedInstance()`. This ensures that we only load the pricing configurations once and reuse them across the application, which is much more efficient and matches the class-based initialization pattern.

I think the root cause is that when a user's memberships change, `DefaultEntityRestCache` needs to verify that the group's event sync state is updated. We should modify `DefaultEntityRestCache.getLastEntityEventBatchForGroup(groupId)` to check if the group is still in the logged-in user's active memberships. If the group is no longer in the user's memberships, it should immediately return `null` and avoid calling the underlying storage. This prevents the application from trying to process or download event batches for groups the user no longer belongs to.

I think the root cause of the inconsistent message handling is that the `_onMessage` handler is blocking the WebSocket receiver loop by awaiting the decryption of entity updates and counter updates. To improve reliability and avoid delays when multiple updates arrive close together, we should update `_onMessage` to handle these updates asynchronously. Specifically, we should trigger `instanceMapper.decryptAndMapToInstance` and then enqueue or process the result in a `.then()` block, but we should not `await` the decryption promise or return it from `_onMessage`. This will allow `_onMessage` to return immediately and keep the message loop responsive.

I think we can simplify the implementation and avoid renaming `AuthHeadersProvider` to `AuthDataProvider` across the entire codebase, which requires updating many files. Since `UserFacade` already has the `isFullyLoggedIn()` method, we should just cast the `_authHeadersProvider` to `UserFacade` in `EntityRestClient` and `ServiceExecutor` when we need to check if the user is fully logged in. This keeps the changes localized to just the client and executor.

I think we should implement `sanitizeInlineAttachment` in `src/misc/HtmlSanitizer.ts` by reusing our existing `sanitizeSVG` method. When the `DataFile` has a MIME type of `image/svg+xml`, we can simply decode the `dirtyFile.data` to a UTF-8 string, run it through `this.sanitizeSVG()`, and then encode the resulting clean text back to a Uint8Array. This avoids duplicating our SVG sanitization rules and keeps the implementation clean and maintainable.

I think the root cause is that `DesktopNetworkClient.executeRequest` resolves the response promise prematurely as soon as headers are received, which causes `downloadNative` to start piping before the socket has fully buffered the incoming data. On slower connections, this race condition leads to stream termination and truncated files, causing the 'Failed to open attachment' error. We should update `executeRequest` in `src/desktop/DesktopNetworkClient.ts` to only resolve the promise after the response stream emits the 'end' event, ensuring the complete payload is buffered before piping.

I think the root cause of the device configuration overwrite on load is that the `_load` method in `DeviceConfig` always calls `_writeToStorage()` when `loadedConfig` is present, even if no changes were made. We should introduce a `modified` flag in `DeviceConfig` to track if any migration actually occurred or if a new `signupToken` was generated. We should then only call `_writeToStorage()` if `modified` is `true`. The existing flat properties and credentials migration logic are correct and do not need to be refactored into a single config object or changed to use constructor parameters for storage.
